title: Presentation invariance of local derived ideal tests
statement: Let e:(Sh(C),R)→(Sh(D),S) be a ringed-topos equivalence with invertible structural map and w a module and derived comparison package tied to e as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-comparison-data]. Let N∈D(S), I be an S-module sheaf and ι:I→S a monomorphism. With local derived ideal completeness of [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], N is locally derived I-complete if and only if w.forward(N) is locally derived w.functor(I)-complete for the inclusion w.functor(ι) followed by the specified rank-one isomorphism. No boundedness or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099J opening presentation reduction, and Tag 0999 definition-derived-complete

proof.text: Replace site-object tests by arbitrary-sheaf tests indexed by generalized sections A→I. Restrict a generalized test to each (U,a) of the element site of A. The restriction-Hom comparison and the sequential-colimit localization comparison identify it with the ordinary local test on U. Thus all its cohomology sheaves vanish at every (U,a); the test object is zero. Conversely use A=h_U# and the site-object module comparison. Empty sites, initial A and empty covering sieves require no exception.

For A=e.inverse(A′), full faithfulness of the sheaf equivalence and the underlying module comparison identify the generalized sections of I′ with those of F(I′). Naturality and the structural regular-unit equation identify the scalar induced by the ideal inclusion. The slice-equivalence restriction squares identify the restricted objects and ideals. The internal-Hom and localization comparisons then identify the two derived test objects up to the slice derived equivalence.

An equivalence preserves and reflects zero objects. Essential surjectivity of e.inverse supplies every test sheaf on the other side, including all its generalized ideal sections. Therefore the arbitrary-sheaf tests hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other. Apply the first step to recover exactly the two site-object completeness conditions.

theorem ringed_equivalence_local_tests
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u}}
    (e : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings R) (localCoefficientRings S))
    [e.inverse.IsEquivalence] [IsIso e.ringMap]
    (w : RingedPresentationAt e)
    (N : PresentationDerived S) (I : PresentationModules S)
    (ι : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit (localCoefficientRings S)) [Mono ι] :
    presentationComplete S I ι N ↔
      presentationComplete R (w.transport.modules.functor.obj I)
        (w.transport.modules.functor.map ι ≫ w.transport.forward.unit.hom)
        (w.transport.forward.derived.obj N)
